articleTitle: Education and industry
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: I have taken as the subject of my address ‘ Education and industry-a general survey.’ I know that the subject is vast and that I can deal with only certain aspects. Many of the ideas put forward are not by any means new, but they are the result of practical experience and personal observation. Some attempt has been made to formulate them into a coherent whole — a skeleton scheme for technical education. Perhaps a more accurate title for this address would be ‘ Some aspects of the relation between technical education and industry.’

articleTitle: Coaxial-cable carrier telephone systems in South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the 960-channel, 4-mega-cycle coaxial-cable carrier telephone system and its application to certain routes in the Union of South Africa. A description of the cable and terminal equipment is followed by a discussion on the facilities provided by the system, the building accommodation, power and test equipment requirements and a brief reference to the special aspects of the installation, testing, performance and maintenance of the 600-channel, 2-6-megacycle system between Pietermaritzburg and Durban which is the first coaxial-cable system to be placed in commercial service in the Southern Hemisphere.

Paine and I participated here in marking the centenary of the discovery of the principle of electromagnetic induction by Michael Faraday, our great original.

articleTitle: Impulse electromagnetic fields
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Expressions are doveloped for the fields established by the Hertzian dipole and by the magnetic dipole in terms of dipole moments. The expressions hold when the derivatives of the dipole moments are continuous for all values of time. It is then assumed that the moment M obeys a hyperbolic tangent law M-tanh(kt) and an insight into the nature of impulsive fields is obtained by considering the condition k-in when the function becomes a step. General expressions for impulse fields are then formulated, and an example is worked to illustrate some properties of impulse fields. It is found that the ‘static,’ ‘induction’ and ‘radiation’ fields have different shapes. Theory also shows that it is meaningless to consider the relative importance of these fields unless a receiver frequency is specified.
